get.summary:
Returns orders with their positions. Every filter is optional and AND-combined. The project
filter accepts several values (repeat the parameter) and matches an order linked to any of them.
The date filters compare the order's own dates, so an order that has none drops out of them —
except validOn, which treats a missing valid-from / expiry as an open bound,
and lastUpdatedOnOrAfter, which also reports changes beneath the order.
get.description: JSON or CSV is chosen by the `Accept` header alone — there is no query parameter for it. `text/csv` returns CSV; `application/json`, a wildcard or no header returns JSON, the default; quality values are honoured. CSV uses ',' as field terminator, \r\n as row terminator, ISO-8601 dates and timestamps, and a fixed column order: OrderID, OrderCode, OrderName, OrderDate, OrderDescription, OrderCurrencyCode, CompanyID, DeliveryDate, ValidFromDate, ExpiryDate, BillingAddress, ShippingAddress, PaymentTerms, ShippingTerms, GoodsRecipient, Notes, ProjectReferenceIDs, OrderRateEntries, OrderCreatorUserID, OrderCreatorEmployeeID, OrderCreatorEmail, OrderCreationDate, OrderLastEditorUserID, OrderLastEditorEmployeeID, OrderLastEditorEmail, OrderLastEditDate, then — with includePositions — OrderPositionID, OrderPositionCode, PositionName, PositionType, FixedPriceAmount, PositionRate, PositionUnit, PositionRateID, PositionRateCode, SoldQuantity, PositionCurrencyCode, SortOrder, PositionCreatorUserID, PositionCreatorEmployeeID, PositionCreatorEmail, PositionCreationDate, PositionLastEditorUserID, PositionLastEditorEmployeeID, PositionLastEditorEmail, PositionLastEditDate, then one trailing column per custom order field named by its column name. In those trailing columns a multi-select renders as its comma-separated labels and a money field as an amount and its ISO currency code (`1500.5 EUR`). Two CSV cells hold a list: `ProjectReferenceIDs` is comma-separated ids, and `OrderRateEntries` is the order's own rate card — prefilled from the framework contract at creation, then editable per order — as comma-separated `Label|Rate|CurrencyCode|Unit` entries in their sort order (a separator inside a label is not escaped, and an entry carries its own currency, which need not match `OrderCurrencyCode`). It is a price list and is independent of the position columns: a position's `PositionRate` is that position's own agreed figure, not necessarily one of these entries. Every creator / editor is flattened into three columns — user id, employee id and email — so the export resolves people without a second call. The position columns `PositionRate` and `PositionUnit` are the legacy work-time price. Pricing moved to per-recording-type rates (see `Order/Position/RecordingTypeRates`), which this export does not carry, so these two may be removed in a future release. `FixedPriceAmount` and `SoldQuantity` are unaffected. Paging counts orders, not CSV rows. `x-row-count` is the number of orders matching the filter, `x-page-row-count` the number of items in this body — orders for JSON, rows for CSV.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Orders to return. Without one this returns every matching order — set it. A negative value is rejected; `0` returns an empty page with `x-row-count: 0` without querying.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of orders to skip, for paging.

parameters.name: includePositions
parameters.description:
Whether each order carries its positions. Default `true`. With `false` the JSON reports
no `positions` and the CSV omits the position columns and returns one row per order — a
cheaper read when only the order headers are wanted. POSTing such a body back leaves the order's
existing positions untouched.

parameters.name: projectReferenceId
parameters.description: Optional project filter by internal id; repeat the parameter for several projects.

parameters.name: projectCode
parameters.description: Optional project filter by code; repeat the parameter for several projects (the ids win when both are given).

parameters.name: validFromOnOrAfter
parameters.description: Only orders whose valid-from date is on or after this day.

parameters.name: validFromOnOrBefore
parameters.description: Only orders whose valid-from date is on or before this day.

parameters.name: expiryOnOrAfter
parameters.description: Only orders whose expiry date is on or after this day (e.g. not yet expired).

parameters.name: expiryOnOrBefore
parameters.description: Only orders whose expiry date is on or before this day.

parameters.name: orderDateOnOrAfter
parameters.description: Only orders whose order date is on or after this day.

parameters.name: orderDateOnOrBefore
parameters.description: Only orders whose order date is on or before this day.

parameters.name: deliveryDateOnOrAfter
parameters.description: Only orders whose delivery date is on or after this day.

parameters.name: deliveryDateOnOrBefore
parameters.description: Only orders whose delivery date is on or before this day.

parameters.name: validOn
parameters.description: Only orders that were valid on this day (valid-from <= day <= expiry, each bound open when unset).

parameters.name: lastUpdatedOnOrAfter
parameters.description: Incremental-sync filter: returns only orders where LastEditDate >= this value. Null means no filter. The order's LastEditDate reports a change to the order or to anything returned beneath it — its positions (added, edited, repriced, removed) and its rate entries — as well as to the position sub-resources served by `Position/RecordingTargets`, `Position/RecordingTypeRates` and `Position/WorkPackages`, which have no such filter of their own. Polling this endpoint and re-fetching the sub-resources of the orders it returns is therefore a complete incremental read, and the highest LastEditDate returned is a safe watermark for the next poll. Each nested position carries its own CreationDate / LastEditDate / Creator / LastEditor, so a consumer can tell which positions moved. A deleted position leaves no row to report, which is why the order's own date moves for it too. Expected format is "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ" (see ISO 8601). Please indicate the timezone ("Z" for UTC), otherwise local time will be assumed.

200.description: The orders — JSON, or CSV when `Accept` asks for `text/csv`.

x-row-count.description: The number of orders matching the filter, not just the current page.

x-page-row-count.description: The number of items in the current response body: orders for JSON, rows for CSV.

monday.description:
Flag to indicate whether Monday should be a working day.
If not provided in the create case, the default is true.

tuesday.description:
Flag to indicate whether Tuesday should be a working day.
If not provided in the create case, the default is true.

wednesday.description:
Flag to indicate whether Wednesday should be a working day.
If not provided in the create case, the default is true.

thursday.description:
Flag to indicate whether Thursday should be a working day.
If not provided in the create case, the default is true.

friday.description:
Flag to indicate whether Friday should be a working day.
If not provided in the create case, the default is true.

saturday.description:
Flag to indicate whether Saturday should be a working day.
If not provided in the create case, the default is false.

sunday.description:
Flag to indicate whether Sunday should be a working day.
If not provided in the create case, the default is false.

mondayHours.description:
The specific working hours for Monday, overriding 'HoursPerDay' for that day.
Ignored when Monday is not a working day. Set to null to fall back to 'HoursPerDay'.

tuesdayHours.description:
The specific working hours for Tuesday, overriding 'HoursPerDay' for that day.
Ignored when Tuesday is not a working day. Set to null to fall back to 'HoursPerDay'.

wednesdayHours.description:
The specific working hours for Wednesday, overriding 'HoursPerDay' for that day.
Ignored when Wednesday is not a working day. Set to null to fall back to 'HoursPerDay'.

thursdayHours.description:
The specific working hours for Thursday, overriding 'HoursPerDay' for that day.
Ignored when Thursday is not a working day. Set to null to fall back to 'HoursPerDay'.

fridayHours.description:
The specific working hours for Friday, overriding 'HoursPerDay' for that day.
Ignored when Friday is not a working day. Set to null to fall back to 'HoursPerDay'.

saturdayHours.description:
The specific working hours for Saturday, overriding 'HoursPerDay' for that day.
Ignored when Saturday is not a working day. Set to null to fall back to 'HoursPerDay'.

sundayHours.description:
The specific working hours for Sunday, overriding 'HoursPerDay' for that day.
Ignored when Sunday is not a working day. Set to null to fall back to 'HoursPerDay'.

WeekDaysInput.description:
Defines the working days of a UserWorkingTimePattern.
If this is not provided in the create case, then the default is Monday to Friday.
Each day can additionally carry specific working hours (e.g. 'MondayHours'): if set,
they override 'HoursPerDay' for that day; if not set, the day uses 'HoursPerDay'.
Specific hours sent for a non-working day are ignored.

dateInWeek.description:
Any date that falls within the planned week. It does not need to be the Monday — it is
normalized to the week (Monday-based) it belongs to when the planning is applied.

hoursPerWeek.description:
The planned effort for the week in hours, where a full standard work week is 40 hours
(e.g. 40 = fully booked for the week, 20 = half a week). A value of 0 removes the planning for this week.

projectTeamMemberID.description:

Decidalo.Domain.Models.WorkPackage.Import.WorkPackageCandidateReferenceInput.BookingID. Must belong to the row's candidate and the work package's project.

bookingID.description:
A booking that, together with the row's candidate and the work package's project, resolves to a
single position. Used only when Decidalo.Domain.Models.WorkPackage.Import.WorkPackageCandidateReferenceInput.ProjectTeamMemberID is not set; an ambiguous or
unresolvable booking is a validation error.

WorkPackageCandidateReferenceInput.description: Optional position selector for a work package candidate assignment. A candidate assignment is a project-team-member position linked to a work package, and a user can be on a work package through several positions (one per booking). This refines which position an import row targets: Decidalo.Domain.Models.WorkPackage.Import.WorkPackageCandidateReferenceInput.ProjectTeamMemberID, when set, targets that exact position.otherwise Decidalo.Domain.Models.WorkPackage.Import.WorkPackageCandidateReferenceInput.BookingID (with the row's candidate) is resolved to a unique position.otherwise the row targets the user's assignment on the work package as a whole (create links one deterministic position; delete removes all of the user's positions on the work package). Used exclusively by the work package candidate import/export round-trip (Decidalo.Import.Host).
